questions.q: Where does a CI-to-CI relationship actually live on the platform?
options: As a free-text note on the CI record
As a record on the cmdb_rel_ci table, connecting a parent CI, a child CI, and a relationship type
Relationships aren't stored; they're inferred automatically from CI names
As a field directly on the cmdb_ci_appl table only
questions.explain: Every relationship is a real row on cmdb_rel_ci, referencing a parent CI, a child CI, and a cmdb_rel_type record.

questions.q: What is a relationship type like "Depends on :: Used by" actually made of?
options: A single generated label the platform computes at query time
A directional pair stored on cmdb_rel_type — one label read from the parent's side, one from the child's side
Two separate, unrelated cmdb_rel_ci records
A category assigned automatically by Discovery with no stored definition
questions.explain: cmdb_rel_type stores both halves of the pair, so the same relationship reads correctly from either CI's point of view.

questions.q: In a "Runs on :: Runs" relationship where an application is the parent and a server is the child, how does it read from the server's side?
options: The server runs the application
The server depends on the application
The server is hosted on the application
The relationship has no meaning from the child's side
questions.explain: "Runs on :: Runs" means the parent runs on the child, and from the child's side, the child runs the parent — so the server runs the application.

questions.q: Why does getting relationship direction backward (e.g., describing a database as "running on" an application) actually matter?
options: It doesn't matter; direction is cosmetic and ignored by every feature
It only affects how the relationship looks in a report, never any calculation
Downstream features like impact analysis and later Change Risk Assessment read the direction to know which CI breaks the other if it goes down — a backward direction gives a wrong or missing answer
ServiceNow automatically corrects reversed relationships on save
questions.explain: Direction encodes the real dependency arrow; later lessons and later courses rely on that arrow being correct to identify real risk.

questions.q: What's the recommended real-world practice before creating a brand-new custom relationship type?
options: Always create a new custom type so it exactly matches the business's own wording
Check whether an existing out-of-box pair (like "Runs on :: Runs" or "Hosted on :: Hosts") already fits the situation
Avoid using cmdb_rel_type entirely and store the relationship as a CI attribute instead
Custom relationship types are not supported on the platform
questions.explain: Reusing the standard set keeps relationship data consistent enough for reports, the Dependency View, and scripts to rely on a known, small vocabulary.
